name: Ian Browne

education.notes: School and degree not disclosed on LinkedIn or in ThinkBusiness interview. Earliest verified role is MSD Quality Control Manager from Apr 2003 — implies tertiary education completed by ~2003.

keyDecisions: Started inside Big Pharma (MSD) managing the software testing and support team for national primary care services — first job sat at the intersection of healthcare and software, not pure pharma.
Spent ~3 years building healthcare-domain credibility before founding.
lessons: A first job inside the industry you later disrupt is a legitimate substitute for a tech or VC CV — especially in regulated verticals like healthcare.
Even inside Big Pharma, gravitating toward the software/IT-adjacent function pre-positions you for a SaaS founding.
careerSteps.notes: Apr 2003 – Apr 2006 (3 yrs 1 mo) per LinkedIn. Managed software testing and support team for national primary care services — directly foreshadows My Surgery Website. This is the 'Big Pharma in London' role referenced in the ThinkBusiness interview.

keyDecisions: Left MSD ~Apr 2006; founded My Surgery Website ~Jan 2007 — short gap from corporate to founder, not a long incubation.
Targeted a fragmented, software-underserved buyer (UK & Ireland GP practices) where willingness-to-pay was small but recurring and defensible.
Scaled to 4,000+ GP-surgery customers and ~20m patient users across UK & Ireland over 8 years before exit.
lessons: Healthcare SaaS into a fragmented buyer base can compound to a multi-thousand-customer book without needing a global hub.
A small geography is not a barrier if your buyers are also distributed (every GP practice is its own buyer).
An 8-year founder run is a normal duration — not the 3-year hype cycle — for a category-defining vertical SaaS exit.
careerSteps.notes: Jan 2007 – Dec 2014 (8 yrs) per LinkedIn. 'Started, developed, designed and sold a software as a service (SAAS) healthcare IT business.' 4,000+ customers, 20m+ patients across UK & Ireland. Acquired by NASDAQ-listed Stericycle; exit value not publicly disclosed.

keyDecisions: Took a short (10-month) post-acquisition operator role at ERS Medical helping 'define and deliver Healthcare IT services in current and future markets' — likely earn-out / transition work tied to the acquirer.
Used the Leeds-based GM role as a bridge year rather than immediately starting a second venture.
lessons: Post-exit founders often have a contractual or transition-period operator role at the acquirer — it isn't a separate career chapter, it's a tail of the founder chapter.
Short stints (<12 months) right after an exit are normal and shouldn't be read as failure.
careerSteps.notes: Jan 2015 – Oct 2015 (10 mos) in Greater Leeds Area per LinkedIn. Almost certainly the transition role following the Stericycle acquisition of My Surgery Website.

keyDecisions: Post-exit, returned to Northern Ireland and joined Ignite as Entrepreneur In Residence (Jan 2018 – Sep 2020) rather than relocating to London / starting a second venture.
Stepped up to Chief Operating Officer (Oct 2020 – Jan 2022) — moved from advisor to operational leadership of NI's flagship pre-seed accelerator.
Optimised for ecosystem leverage — Ignite founders collectively raised £100m+ in venture capital.
lessons: Post-exit, building local founder infrastructure compounds the next generation rather than competing with it.
EIR → COO is a credible 'soft re-entry' pattern: start as advisor, escalate to operator once the fit is proven.
In a small ecosystem an exited founder who stays disproportionately shapes the next cohort.
careerSteps.notes: Two consecutive Ignite roles per LinkedIn: EIR Jan 2018 – Sep 2020 (2 yrs 9 mos) then COO Oct 2020 – Jan 2022 (1 yr 4 mos), 4 yrs 1 mo total. Belfast, NI.

keyDecisions: Took first publicly visible NED seat on a NI healthcare-staffing software company — replays the My Surgery Website thesis (healthcare + SaaS + UK/Ireland buyers) as a board member rather than founder.
lessons: Post-exit, NED seats in your domain of strength (healthcare SaaS) are an early way to stay in the game without being CEO again.
Board seats stack — they are part-time and accumulate alongside an operator role.
careerSteps.notes: Jan 2017 – Feb 2020 (3 yrs 2 mos) per LinkedIn. Overlaps with Ignite EIR — confirms NED + EIR + COO can run in parallel.

keyDecisions: Took a second NED seat on a NI consumer/loyalty fintech — diversified board portfolio beyond healthcare into NI tech more broadly.
lessons: Second NED is signal that the first one went well — boards beget boards.
Multi-year board seats (5+ yrs) are normal; they aren't quick rotations.
careerSteps.notes: Aug 2019 – Jan 2025 (5 yrs 6 mos) per LinkedIn. Belfast Metropolitan Area.

keyDecisions: Left Ignite COO (Jan 2022) and took NDRC MD (May 2022) — a step up from NI-only to all-island Irish ecosystem leadership.
Ran the 5-year, €17m NDRC accelerator across Dogpatch Labs (Dublin), Portershed (Galway), Republic of Work (Cork), RDI Hub (Kerry).
lessons: An exited founder is highly hireable into national ecosystem-leadership roles — operator credibility transfers to programme leadership.
The NI → all-Ireland step is a real career ladder rung for ecosystem builders, not just for founders.
careerSteps.notes: May 2022 – Apr 2025 (3 yrs) per LinkedIn. Dublin-based. €17m / 5-year NDRC contract per ThinkBusiness.

keyDecisions: Took NED seat at Eolas Medical (Belfast healthcare-SaaS) the same month he founded Founder Labs — explicitly returning to a healthcare-SaaS board now that there's bandwidth.
lessons: Board portfolios cycle — as one NED ends (Locate a Locum 2020, loyalBe 2025) another begins.
Re-entering healthcare via the board, not the founder seat, lets you keep optionality while running a new venture.
careerSteps.notes: Jan 2024 – Present per LinkedIn. Started concurrently with Founder Labs CEO role.

keyDecisions: Founded Founder Labs (Jan 2024) ~16 months before stepping out of NDRC (Apr 2025) — built the next thing inside the safety of the day job rather than burning a bridge.
Building a NI-based programme helping founders 'build, sell, scale and raise' with global ambition — productising ~17 years of post-exit ecosystem work.
Continues to be NI-based rather than relocating after exit / ecosystem roles.
lessons: A career can layer founder → ecosystem operator → second founder of ecosystem infrastructure itself.
Overlap the new venture with the old role — Jan 2024 founding + Apr 2025 NDRC exit shows 15 months of paid runway while building the next thing.
Geographic loyalty is a viable career thesis — staying somewhere compounds soft power that relocating burns.
careerSteps.notes: Jan 2024 – Present per LinkedIn. Belfast Metropolitan Area. Full-time CEO since Apr 2025 (post-NDRC exit). Programme positioning per landing page: 'global ambition from Northern Ireland.'

exitEvents.notes: My Surgery Website acquired by NASDAQ-listed Stericycle. Likely late 2014 / early 2015 given the LinkedIn handover (My Surgery Website ended Dec 2014, ERS Medical 'General Manager, Healthcare IT' started Jan 2015). Exit value not publicly disclosed.

outcomes.currentStatus: Belfast-based. CEO of Founder Labs (full-time since Apr 2025). NED at Eolas Medical. Earlier: 3 yrs MD of NDRC (€17m all-island Irish accelerator), 4 yrs at Ignite (EIR then COO), exited My Surgery Website to Stericycle.

lessons.lesson: You can build a real outcome from Northern Ireland if your buyer base is also distributed (e.g. GP surgeries across UK & Ireland).
lessons.source: Inferred from My Surgery Website trajectory — ThinkBusiness interview + LinkedIn dates.

lessons.lesson: Big Pharma (MSD) → healthcare-SaaS founder is a credible NI-to-exit path; ~3 years inside the industry buys you the domain credibility a tech-hub CV would otherwise provide.
lessons.source: LinkedIn (MSD Apr 2003 – Apr 2006 → My Surgery Website Jan 2007).

lessons.lesson: Post-exit, ecosystem-building in your home region (Ignite, NDRC, Founder Labs) can be a multi-decade career — 10+ years and counting since the 2014 exit.
lessons.source: LinkedIn trajectory across Ignite (2018-2022), NDRC (2022-2025), Founder Labs (2024-).

lessons.lesson: Overlap your next thing with your current paid role — Browne founded Founder Labs in Jan 2024 while still running NDRC until Apr 2025.
lessons.source: LinkedIn date overlap between NDRC MD and Founder Labs CEO.

lessons.lesson: Stack NED seats alongside the day job — they compound network, cash, and optionality without being a separate career.
lessons.source: LinkedIn: Locate a Locum (2017-2020), loyalBe (2019-2025), Eolas Medical (2024-) all ran during Ignite/NDRC tenure.
